routine.title: Daily Rhythm of Student Activities
routine.subtitle: A structured daily flow from morning to afternoon integrating Islamic etiquette, Quranic halaqah, and academic exploration.
routine.slot1Description: Students are welcomed by teachers at the school gate, neatly arrange their shoes, perform ablution, and observe congregational Dhuha prayer in the prayer hall.
routine.slot1Mentor: Supervising teachers greet at the gate and mentors lead morning prayers.
routine.slot2Subtitle: Prime Morning Memorization and Retention Session
routine.slot2Description: Small halaqah groups guided through progressive talaqqi method, phonetic articulation, new memorization recitation, and systematic revision.
routine.slot2Mentor: Mentors listen to each student's recitation with personalized attention.
routine.slot3Subtitle: National Curriculum Integrated with Inquiry Learning
routine.slot3Description: Interactive indoor and outdoor learning combining literacy, applied mathematical numeracy, and natural science inquiry.
routine.slot3Mentor: Homeroom teachers actively facilitate discussions and experiments.
routine.slot4Title: Mindful Lunch and Congregational Dhuhr Prayer
routine.slot4Description: Proper handwashing, seated dining with etiquette and prayers, self-tidying meal trays, followed by orderly ablution and congregational Dhuhr prayer.
routine.slot4Mentor: Teachers accompany students throughout lunch and congregational prayer.
routine.slot5Subtitle: Practical Arabic and English with Extracurriculars
routine.slot5Description: Reinforcing daily conversational Arabic and English vocabulary, combined with talent exploration such as calligraphy, basic robotics, and archery.
routine.slot5Mentor: Specialist instructors guide hands-on practice in a safe environment.
routine.slot6Title: Daily Reflection, Closing Prayers, and Dismissal
routine.slot6Subtitle: Reviewing Daily Achievements Before Heading Home
routine.slot6Description: Students organize their learning supplies independently, reflect on the day's achievements with homeroom teachers, pray, and dismiss orderly to parents.
routine.slot6Mentor: Homeroom teachers hand over students directly to verified guardians.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Admissions and Schooling
faq.subtitle: Clear official answers regarding entry readiness, Quran memorization, and new student matriculation.
faq.q1: Are prospective students required to be fluent in reading, writing, and arithmetic before admission?
faq.a1: No. The admission observation does not enforce rigid pass-fail reading, writing, or math tests. It uses guided playful activities to map fine motor skills, emotional maturity, and foundational independence.
faq.q2: What if a prospective student is not yet familiar with Arabic letters or fluent in Iqra?
faq.a2: Al-Birru conducts an intensive phonics matriculation program at the start of the semester. Teachers guide students patiently from fundamental letters using personalized talaqqi without judgment.
faq.q3: How is the target of 3 juz memorization with verified sanad evaluated?
faq.a3: Each student maintains a daily memorization tracking logbook. Evaluation is conducted through daily recitation, weekly revision, and public single-sitting tasmi tests before teachers and parents.
faq.q4: How does the school ensure energy balance and comfort during integrated school hours?
faq.a4: The daily schedule balances cognitive focus (morning halaqah and science) with active rest (healthy dining and congregational prayer) and motor exploration in spacious green open grounds.
